title: Stationary-cue response versus retained activity
role: Complementary whole-grid characterization of the same 80conditions; composition remains open.

assets.caption: Direct withdrawal/retention pairs at every requested angle and duration.

legend: Cue withdrawal versus retained activity orientation in the same standardized-angle stationary-cue experiment. A–D, The open point is measured at cue withdrawal and the filled point after 13,000 cue-free native time units; thin vertical segments connect each pair, dashed curves connect withdrawal points and solid curves connect retained points. Four shared colours denote prepared-axis cue-centre offsets 180°/90°/45°/22.5°; dotted lines mark the exact targets in P coordinates. Every one of the 80 conditions remains, including 35 initial cue–core overlaps, with the exact same basals, fixed physical cue supports and native dose/time protocols as the standardized-angle checkpoint. The displayed activity angle is arg P for physical P=M₁(t)/M₁(0), masked at R < 0.1. In the paired magnitude/amount support sheet, R is distinguished from physical total activity M₀(t)/M₀(0); translucent envelopes span sampled minima/maxima over the full history and are not error bands. The square outline flags the independently measured full-field tail-gate failure at Holmes 180° / T300; four compact reuses have no full-field qualification. Cue-on deflection can relax back toward the original state or progress further toward the cue after withdrawal. No refined minimum-duration claim, ancestry inference or movement law is assigned.
